alignments.note: Rule 81: preposition fused with its governed pronoun into a single English *there-* word; *there-* answers to the pronoun and *-with* to `ἐν`, so the pair is one `aligned` unit headed on the pronominal, not `noncompositional` under rule 45. Rule 81's own examples `ἐν αὐτῷ` → *therein* and `δι᾽ αὐτῆς` → *thereby* are pronominals, so the rule reaches a personal pronoun and not only a demonstrative.
Rule 9: the inflected verb takes its English subject pronoun; the lexical verb is the head. The ASV's inversion *bless we* is English word order and does not move the head (rule 17).
Rule 19: the article surfaces as *the*. The packet gloss *our* is not what the ASV wrote, and no English possessive stands here to displace it under rule 20 or to be recovered under rule 76.
Rule 26: the noun is independently recoverable and is split from its article.
The second coordinated noun stands bare; the single article governs the whole phrase and has already taken *the*.
Rule 81 again, as with s001–s002; the ASV repeats the portmanteau and the analysis is the same one (rule 24).
Rule 9: subject pronoun rides with the verb, headed on the lexical verb *curse*.
Rule 23: the ASV gives *men* no determiner, so the article has no English realization. Rule 13 forbids grouping it with its noun for convenience.

Rule 31: the article follows an expressed head noun (`ἀνθρώπους`) and a participle follows it, so the participle carries the supplied relativizer and copula and the second attributive article is its own `unrepresented` unit under rule 23. The competing reading would give *who* to the article under rule 32 or rule 90, but both are scoped to a substantival article governing no head noun, which is not the case here. Rule 31's prepositional-phrase carve-out does not reach this either: `καθ᾽ ὁμοίωσιν θεοῦ` sits inside the participial phrase, and the participle is the verb that carries the relativizer.
Rule 36: the English preposition governing the phrase realizes the Greek preposition.

Rule 51's anarthrous clause: no Greek article stands here, so the supplied *the* is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the noun it determines, and the noun is the head. Rule 21 has no article to anchor the determiner, so *the* does not ride with `καθ᾽`.
Rule 17: for a source noun rendered by *of + noun*, the noun is the head; the *of* realizes the genitive and rides with it, no article standing to anchor it (rule 21).

Rule 31: the attributive participle is recast as a finite relative clause, so the relativizer *who* and the copula *are* are its helpers under rules 7 and 9, headed on the lexical participle *made* rather than on the copula (rule 17). Rule 15 permits the unit's distance from `καθ᾽ ὁμοίωσιν θεοῦ`, which keeps its own English words.

review_notes: Reviewed unchanged: every unit of the accepted alignment survives review. The partition is complete — all 18 source and all 20 target ids appear exactly once.

Both `ἐν αὐτῇ` phrases go to rule 81 (`aligned`, headed on the pronoun) rather than rule 45 `noncompositional`, since *-with* answers to the preposition and *there-* to the pronoun. Rule 81's cited units include `ἐν αὐτῷ` → *therein* and `δι᾽ αὐτῆς` → *thereby*, both governing personal pronouns, so the rule is not confined to demonstratives.
s004 takes *the* despite the packet gloss *our*: no English possessive is written, so rules 20 and 76 do not arise.
s012 and s014 are both `unrepresented` for different reasons — no determiner written for *men* (rule 23), and an article after an expressed head noun with a participle following (rule 31).

A reference comparison may report s014 as represented if it reads *who* off the article; rule 31's expressed-head-noun test is what decides against that, and rule 90 says in terms that it blesses no unit in which a head noun is expressed.

s016's supplied *the* stays on `ὁμοίωσιν` and does not ride with `καθ᾽`: the Greek is anarthrous, so rule 51's anarthrous clause makes the determiner a rule 7 helper on the word it determines, and rule 21 has no article here to carry a case preposition.
